decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) 1 September 2020, or any amending Order, the premises shall only be used as storage/light industrial and shall not be used for any other purpose besides Use Class B2 (General Industrial) and B8 (Storage or distribution), or for any other purpose without the express written permission of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: In the interest of ensuring the effective control of the premises for the uses applied.

(a) Prior to the commencement of the development (excluding demolition and site preparation), the following details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority:i. External facing materials including sample boards of all facing materials and finishes as well as sample panels;ii. Landscape materials, including paving and hard surfacing materials, and any boundary treatments, including edging and planters;iii. External rainwater goods;iii. Typical sectional drawings at 1:20 through all typical external elements/facades, including all openings in external walls including doors and window-type reveals, window heads and window sills (including fixing details);iv. Sectional and elevational drawings at 1:20 (where considered relevant) of junctions between different external materials, parapets to roofs, photovoltaic arrays, roofs of cores, canopies, entrance areas, doors and where buildings meet the ground;v. Roof details;vi. Details of any rooftop plant, extract ducts and fans;vii. Plans of ground floor entrance cores at 1:20, elevations of entrance doors at 1:10 and details of entrance door thresholds;viii. All external metalwork including handrails and fencing;ix. external bin storage facilities; andxi. Confirmation from an accredited fire engineer that the materials complied with the approved Fire Strategy Statement.xii. Details shall be consistent with the approved Design and Access Statement and/or references to materials in approved drawings.xiii. A signage strategy including materials, projection, 1:10 detailed drawings and                  details  of illumination as appropriate, (b) The required sample board(s) shall be made available on site for consideration by the Local Planning Authority and approved sample board(s) shall be retained on site for the duration of the construction of the building to which they relate.The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance in accordance with policy D4 of the London Plan, CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD37 of the Enfield Development Management Policy(2014).

Prior to the commencement of development above ground works, full details of the surfacing materials to be used within the development including footpaths, parking areas and road markings (where applicable) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The surfacing shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details before the development is occupied or use commences.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory visual appearance and in the in interests of highways safety.

Prior to the occupation of the development, details of a landscaping scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  The landscaping scheme shall include the following details: 1.	Schedules of plants to include native and wildlife friendly species and large canopy plants in appropriate locations (noting species, planting sizes and proposed numbers / densities) to be planted;2.	soft plantings: including grass and turf areas, shrub and herbaceous areas;All landscaping in accordance with the approved scheme shall be completed/planted in full during the first planting season following practical completion of the development hereby approved.  The landscaping planting shall set out a plan for the continued management and maintenance of the site and any planting which dies, becomes severely damaged or diseased within five years of completion of the development shall be replaced with new planting in accordance with the approved details or an approved alternative and to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details so approved and shall be maintained as such thereafter. Reason: To minimise the impact of the development on the ecological value of the area, to ensure the development provides the maximum possible provision towards the creation of habitats and valuable areas for biodiversity and to preserve the character and appearance of the area.

Notwithstanding the submitted plans, prior to completion or first occupation of the development hereby approved, whichever is the sooner; full details of all proposed tree planting shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include:a) planting and maintenance specifications, including cross-section drawings, use of guards or other protective measures and confirmation of location;b) species and sizes, nursery stock type, supplier and defect period. All tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with those details and at those times;c) tree pit design (where appropriate) and;d) underground modular systems (where appropriate).e) How the proposed tree planting is compatible with the drainage strategy and other utilities.Any trees that are found to be dead, dying, severely damaged or diseased within five years of the completion of the building works OR five years of the carrying out of the landscaping scheme (whichever is later), shall be replaced in the next planting season by specimens of similar size and species in the first suitable planting season.Reason: To ensure that the aesthetic and ecological value of the site is enhanced post development in line with the Biodiversity Action Plan, Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy, Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and the London Plan (2021).

Notwithstanding the details set out in the submitted Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Strategy (Ref 40312-BGL-XX-XX-RP-D-0001), 17 June 2025, prior to the commencement of any construction work (excluding demolition and site preparation), details of the Sustainable Drainage Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and must conform with the Landscaping Strategy. The details shall include:Sizes, storage volumes, cross-sections, long-sections (where appropriate) and specifications of all the source control SuDS measures including rain gardens, raised planters, green roofs, swale and permeable paving, final sizes, storage volumes, invert levels, cross-sections and specifications of all site control.SuDS measures including ponds, soakaways and underground tanks. Include calculations demonstrating functionality where relevant.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 61 and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan (2021) and the NPPF (2026).

Prior to commencement of any development (excluding demolition and site preparation) an Energy Statement shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that the development is compliant with the [London Plan 2021] or subsequent versions requirements to achieve net zero through the measures taken in Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the Energy hierarchy to reduce carbon emitted from the operation of a development and its services, and the calculated New Development Carbon Compensation to be paid for the remaining emissions. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details. Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy SI 2 of the New London Plan 2021 and Policy SE2-SE4 of the emerging Enfield Local Plan 2019-2041 expected to be adopted early 2026.

The development hereby approved will be carried out according to the Energy Statement date [FUTURE DATE] submitted by [HOARE LEA] demonstrating or better. Following the practical completion of the development, an updated Energy Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, reflecting the measures taken in practice in Be Lean, Be Clean and Be Green stages of the Energy hierarchy to reduce carbon emitted from the operation of a development and its services, as committed to in the design stage, and the amended Further New Development Carbon Compensation to be paid for the remaining emissions.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy SI 2 of the New London Plan 2021 and Policy SE2-SE4 of the emerging Enfield Local Plan 2019-2041 expected to be adopted early 2026.

Prior to commencement of any development (excluding demolition and site preparation), an overheating strategy shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority including the complete result table. The approved strategy shall be implemented prior to first occupation and maintained on site.Reason: To ensure that suitable living conditions are achieved within the development and that the buildings do not overheat, in accordance with policy SI4 of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby approved shall achieve a BREEAM rating of 'Excellent' or an equivalent independent measure of energy performance and sustainability. Where the performance of the development is measured using BREEAM, it shall achieve not less than the total credits for each of the Energy, Materials and Waste categories in the BREEAM Pre-Assessment hereby approved. A post completion certificate (or equivalent certification) confirming that the development has been completed in accordance with the required BREEAM rating and has maintained or exceeded the approved total credit scores for each of the Energy, Materials and Waste categories, shall be submitted to us for our approval within three months of first occupation of the development. Reason: To ensure that the development achieves the highest levels of sustainable design and construction in accordance with DMD51 of the Development Management Document (2014) and Policy SI 2 of the New London Plan (2021).

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby permitted (excluding demolition and site preparation), the details, including siting, of the Electric Vehicle Charging Points to be installed shall be provided to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. All electric charging points shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of any of the residential units hereby permitted.Reason: To ensure that the development complies with the sustainable development policy requirements of the London Plan (2021).

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the 6 long-stay and 3 short-stay cycle parking spaces have been fully constructed in accordance with the hereby approved details and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

The development shall not be brought into use until the application for removal of the redundant dropped kerb has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This condition should be read in conjunction with the Informative also attached to the permission.Reason: To ensure the development conforms with Enfield DMD Policy 46.

No development shall take place until a Construction Management Plan, written in accordance with the Mayor of London's supplementary planning guidance 'The Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' detailing how dust, emissions and traffic will be managed during demolition and construction work shall be submitted to the local planning authority for approval. The statement should also include:a) photographic condition survey of public carriageways, verges and footways in the vicinity of the site;b) map showing routeing of demolition and construction vehicles to/from the site;c) access arrangements for deliveries to the site;d) wheel cleaning methodology and facilities or measures to keep the highway clear of mud and debris.For the avoidance of doubt, this condition can be discharged either:a. Prior to the commencement of demolition works, with details relating solely to demolition activities; and subsequently b. Prior to the commencement of construction works, with details relating solely to construction activities; Or c. Prior to the commencement of development, through the submission of a single Construction Management Plan covering both demolition and construction.  The approved Construction Management Plan shall be fully implemented for the duration of the demolition and construction works and shall be adhered to unless agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers, minimise dust and emissions, ensure highway safety, and protect the character and appearance of the area during demolition and construction in accordance with the Development Plan and the Mayor of London's guidance on construction impacts.

No part of the development shall be occupied until a site wide Delivery and Servicing Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This shall then be implemented as approved and remain in operation for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In order to ensure that deliveries and servicing of the site is managed effectively so as to minimise impact upon the road network and to safeguard the amenities of the occupiers of residential properties and in the interests of road safety.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until a Certificate of Compliance in accordance with Secured by Design - Residential Guide 2025 (or the relevant Secured by Design Guide(s) or an achieved Crime Prevention Standard) has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Metropolitan Police or Local Planning Authority.  The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained.Reason: In the interest of creating safer, secure, sustainable communities.

Prior to the commencement of the development (excluding demolition and site preparation), details for the siting and maintenance of a minimum of 2 permanent bat and bird roosting boxes within the facades and roof edges of built structures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Roosting boxes shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to first use.Reason: To ensure that the development contributes to improving the ecology and biodiversity of the area, in accordance with the NPPF (2026), London Plan (2021), policy CP36 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010) and DMD79 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014)

All areas of the sire where birds may nest that are to be removed as part of the development, are to be cleared outside the bird-nesting season (March - August inclusive) or if clearance during the bird-nesting season cannot reasonably be avoided, a suitably qualified ecologist will check the areas to be removed immediately prior to clearance and advise whether nesting birds are present.  If active nests are recorded, no clearance or other works that may disturb active nests shall proceed until all young have fledged the nest. Reason:  To ensure that wildlife is not adversely impacted by the proposed development in accordance with national wildlife legislation and in line with CP36 of the Core Strategy.  Nesting birds are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act, 1981 (as amended).

Prior to commencement of the development (excluding demolition and site preparation), an updated Fire Statement shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing. The Fire Statement shall be produced by an independent third party suitably qualified assessor and shall detail the building's construction, methods, products and materials used; the means of escape for all building users including those who are disabled or require level access together with the associated management plan; access for fire service personnel and equipment; plan showing the location of the nearest dry risers, ongoing maintenance and monitoring and how provision will be made within the site to enable fire appliances to gain access to the building. The development shall be carried out in strict accordance with the details approved for the life time of the development.Reason: To comply with Policy D12 of the London Plan (2021).

Prior to the commencement of development, a detailed Construction Site Waste Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan should include as a minimum:a. How the promotion of a more circular economy has been undertaken, which improves resource efficiency and innovation to keep products and materials at their highest use for as long as possible;b. How waste minimisation and waste prevention has been encouraged through the reuse of materials and using fewer resources in the production and distribution of products;c. How the development performs regarding re-use and recycling rates for construction, demolition and excavation waste; andd. How performance of all of the above will be monitored and reported.For the avoidance of doubt, this condition can be discharged either:a. Prior to the commencement of demolition works, with details relating solely to demolition activities; and subsequently b. Prior to the commencement of construction works, with details relating solely to construction activities; Or c. Prior to the commencement of development, through the submission of a single Construction Site Waste Management Plan covering both demolition and construction. The approved Site Waste Management Plan shall be fully implemented for the duration of the demolition and construction works and shall be adhered to unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Prior to occupation, a detailed Site Waste Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan should include as a minimum:i.) How the development contributes toward ensuring the minimising of biodegradable or recyclable waste to landfill and meets or exceeds the municipal waste recycling target of 65 per cent;ii.) Details of waste segregation proposals; andiii.) Waste storage and collection proposals.The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To maximise the amount of waste diverted from landfill consistent with the waste hierarchy and to accord with Policy SI 7 of the New London Plan (2021), Policy DMD57 of the Development Management Document (2014).

1. Prior to the commencement of the development, evidence of site registration at http://nrmm.london/ to allow continuing details of Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) and plant of net power between 37kW and 560 kW to be uploaded during the construction phase of the development shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.2. Evidence that all plant and machinery to be used during the demolition and construction phases of the development shall meets Stage IV of EU Directive 97/68/ EC for both NOx and PM emissions shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority.3. During the course of the demolitions, site preparation and construction phases, an inventory and emissions records for all Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) shall be kept on site. The inventory shall demonstrate that all NRMM is regularly serviced and detail proof of emission limits for all equipment. All documentation shall be made available for inspection by Local Authority officers at all times until the completion of the development.Reasons: In the interests of good air quality and to protect public health with regard to London Plan (2021).

No occupation of the development shall take place until an acoustic report, written in line with the methodology in BS4142:2014+A1 2019, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from the combined mechanical plant and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the combined plant does not exceed a level of 5dB below the typical measured background noise level measured as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest or most noise affected residential property.Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance.

Prior to occupation of the development, a lighting strategy detailing the lighting around the perimeter of the building shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall include details of the location, specification, and direction of any external artificial lighting and it must be considerate to potential bat roosting at the east elevation of the building. The approved lighting shall be provided in accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the development. Reason: In order to ensure a safe environment for future occupants and visitors to the site, to reduce the risk of crime and to protect natural habitats.

Not withstanding the granted permission, the current or future occupiers at the site are prohibited from making new gas connections to the site to prioritise heat decarbonisation at this location and to facilitate a connection of the site to the borough-wide district heating network (Energetik).Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policies DMD51-54 of the Development Management Document (2014), Policy SI 2 of the New London Plan 2021 and Policy SE1 of the emerging Enfield Local Plan 2019-2041 expected to be adopted early 2026.

The granted development shall not be operational as a Use Class B2/B8 facility before 07:00am or after 7:00pm Monday to Friday or before 07:00am and after 1:00pm on Saturday. Reason: To safeguard the amenities of the occupiers of nearby residential properties in view of Appendix 5 (Commercial Opening Hours) of the Development Management Document (2014).
